body.statement: Supporting compact-face lemma. For every nonempty compact fiber \(\mathcal K(p)\), \(L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\le L(p)\le U(p)\le U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\). Moreover, \(L(p)=L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) if and only if \(\mathfrak F^-(p)\ne\varnothing\), and \(U(p)=U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) if and only if \(\mathfrak F^+(p)\ne\varnothing\). Empty common minimizing or maximizing faces therefore imply, respectively, \(\Delta^-(p)>0\) or \(\Delta^+(p)>0\).
body.justification: This compact-set identity supplies the geometric criterion used by the strict-containment obligation; it is supporting machinery, not a headline result.
body.gap: The identity is an elementary min-of-a-sum fact on a compact set, so no field-level novelty is claimed.
body.consumer: The exact two-stage analysis can certify strict containment by proving that one of the two common-face intersections is empty.
